technical.clientSecretHandling: Web (confidential) apps send client_secret (URL-encoded, or HTTP Basic) or a signed certificate assertion (client_assertion) to the token endpoint. Prefer certificates over secrets in production. Public clients (SPA, native) must not use a secret. Use PKCE for all app types, including confidential web apps.

refreshTokens.expiry: 90 days by default (24 hours for SPA redirect URIs). Not configurable through token lifetime policies since January 30, 2021; can be revoked earlier.
refreshTokens.notes: Only returned when offline_access is requested. Each refresh returns a new refresh token: store it and discard the old one (the old one isn't revoked). Refresh tokens are bound to user + client, not to a tenant or resource.

technical.accessTokenLifetime: Random 60-90 minutes (75 on average); read expires_in from the token response. CAE-capable clients may get tokens lasting 20-28 hours.
redirectUriRules: Must exactly match a redirect URI registered on the app's Authentication page (case-sensitive path)
HTTPS required; http allowed only for localhost
For localhost the port is ignored when matching
Max 256 redirect URIs for work/school-only apps (100 if personal accounts are also supported); max 256 characters each
No special characters ! $ ' ( ) , ; and no internationalized domain names
Query parameters allowed only for apps that sign in work or school accounts only

profiles.intent: Read mail and calendar from users in other organizations (multi-tenant)

scopes.name: https://graph.microsoft.com/Mail.Read
scopes.purpose: Read the signed-in user's mailbox (GET /me/messages). Admin consent required: No in the Graph reference, but many tenants still block user consent to it (see nuances).

scopes.name: https://graph.microsoft.com/Calendars.Read
scopes.purpose: Read events in the user's calendars (GET /me/events). Admin consent required: No in the Graph reference; also on the Microsoft-managed policy's exclusion list.

scopes.name: offline_access
scopes.purpose: Get a refresh token. Admin consent required: No.

scopes.name: User.Read
scopes.purpose: Sign in and read the user's profile; added to new registrations automatically. Admin consent required: No.

scopes.name: openid
scopes.purpose: Optional: returns an ID token so you learn who signed in and their tenant (tid). Admin consent required: No.

testModeLimits.text: There is no test or development mode. A new registration works immediately for any tenant whose admin (or, where allowed, user) consents. Your own new tenant probably uses the Microsoft-managed consent policy too, so expect to consent as an admin when testing.

configGotchas.text: Choose Multiple Entra ID tenants (also labelled Accounts in any organizational directory) and use /organizations or /common, not your tenant ID, in the authorize and token URLs.
Add offline_access to the scope or you get no refresh token.
Register the callback under the Web platform, not Single-page application. SPA-type redirect URIs get 24-hour refresh tokens and need an Origin header.
Client secrets last at most 24 months. Track the expiry or move to a certificate.

stage1.summary: Self-serve: register a multitenant app in the Microsoft Entra admin center, add a Web redirect URI, a secret and Graph delegated permissions, then complete one code flow.

stage2.summary: No app review for delegated Graph access. The real gate is consent in each customer tenant: the default policy for new tenants blocks user consent to Mail.Read and Calendars.Read, so a customer admin must grant it. Publisher verification is optional, needs a verified AI Cloud Partner Program account, and usually takes 3-5 business days.

time.range: 3-5 business days for Partner Center business verification (only if you pursue publisher verification); then minutes to mark the app verified. Per-tenant admin consent depends on each customer; no documented time.
time.startsWhen: when you submit the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program enrollment

stage1DoneWhen.text: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages?$select=sender,subject and GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/events?$select=subject,start,end with Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN both return 200 with a value array, and your token response included a refresh_token.

blockedBy.how: Each customer tenant decides whether users may consent. Under the Microsoft-managed default (new tenants), users can't consent to Mail.Read or Calendars.Read, so an admin must grant consent. Admins can also turn off user consent completely, require user assignment, or leave risk-based step-up on, which sends unverified multitenant apps to admin approval.
Risk-based step-up consent (on by default) treats consent to newly registered, unverified multitenant apps asking for non-basic permissions as risky and requires admin approval (AADSTS90094).

Without a verified Partner Program account, a non-onmicrosoft.com publisher domain and the right Entra and Partner Center roles, you can't become a verified publisher, and the consent prompt keeps showing Unverified.

profiles.bottomLine: You can get a first token in one sitting. For other organizations, plan on admin consent in every customer tenant: the default consent policy for new tenants excludes Mail.Read and Calendars.Read from user consent. Publisher verification removes the Unverified label and helps where tenants allow user consent, but it needs a business-verified Partner Program account.
topRisks: Users in customer tenants hit Need admin approval and can't connect until an admin consents
Publisher verification needs a legally registered business and a custom domain, which solo developers may not have
A client secret expires after at most 24 months and silently breaks every connection

steps.title: Register a multitenant app in the Microsoft Entra admin center
instructions: Sign in to https://entra.microsoft.com as at least an Application Developer. Use a work or school (Entra) account, because apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can't be publisher verified later.
If you have several tenants, use the Settings icon in the top menu to switch to the tenant that should own the app. The registration can't be moved to another tenant later.
Browse to Entra ID > App registrations and select New registration.
Enter a Name (users see it, and you can change it later).

Under Supported account types choose Multiple Entra ID tenants. Older Microsoft pages call this option Accounts in any organizational directory. Pick Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts only if you also want Outlook.com users, which lowers the redirect URI limits.
Select Register, then copy the Application (client) ID from the Overview page.

steps.title: Add a Web redirect URI
instructions: In the app registration, under Manage select Authentication.
On the Redirect URI configuration tab select Add Redirect URI, then choose the Web tile (server-side apps), not Single-page application.
Enter your callback URL exactly as your code sends it, then select Configure.
Use HTTPS. http is allowed only for localhost, and the localhost port is ignored when matching. Don't register several localhost URIs that differ only by port.
Keep dev and prod redirect URIs in separate registrations if you can.

steps.title: Add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions
instructions: Select API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Delegated permissions.
Under Select permissions, select Mail.Read, Calendars.Read and offline_access (and openid if you want an ID token). User.Read is already there by default.
Select Add permissions. These become the app's configured (required) permissions, which the admin consent flow uses.
Mail.ReadBasic is the least-privileged permission for listing messages. Use it instead of Mail.Read if you don't need bodies or attachments.

steps.title: Create a client secret (or upload a certificate)
instructions: Select Certificates & secrets > Client secrets > New client secret.
Add a description and pick an expiration: 24 months maximum, under 12 recommended.
Select Add and copy the secret Value right away, because it's never shown again. Store it only on your server or in a secret manager.
For production, prefer a certificate (Certificates > Upload certificate, .cer/.pem/.crt) over a secret.

steps.title: Send yourself through the authorize URL
instructions: Open https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&response_type=code&redirect_uri=URL_ENCODED_URI&response_mode=query&scope=offline_access%20https%3A%2F%2Fgraph.microsoft.com%2FMail.Read%20https%3A%2F%2Fgraph.microsoft.com%2FCalendars.Read%20https%3A%2F%2Fgraph.microsoft.com%2FUser.Read&state=RANDOM&code_challenge=CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256
Use /organizations for work or school accounts only, or /common if you also support personal accounts. Don't put your own tenant ID here.
Sign in and consent. If your tenant uses the Microsoft-managed consent default, a non-admin test user gets Need admin approval, so test as an admin or grant admin consent first.
Microsoft redirects back with code and state. Check that state matches. The code expires after about 1 minute.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
instructions: POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded to https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/oauth2/v2.0/token with client_id, grant_type=authorization_code, code, the same redirect_uri, code_verifier and client_secret (URL-encoded), or client_assertion_type + client_assertion for a certificate.
Store access_token, expires_in and refresh_token. Access tokens last 60-90 minutes.
Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token (plus client_secret). Each refresh returns a new refresh token: save it and discard the old one.
Treat Graph access tokens as opaque. Don't decode or validate them in your code.

steps.title: Check the token works against Outlook mail and calendar
instructions: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages?$select=sender,subject with Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN and expect 200 with a value array (10 messages per page by default).
GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/events?$select=subject,start,end and expect 200 with a value array. Times are in UTC unless you send Prefer: outlook.timezone.
Page with the full @odata.nextLink URL. Don't build $skip yourself.

steps.title: Give customer admins a way to grant tenant-wide consent
instructions: Build a connect page that sends the customer's admin to https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=CLIENT_ID&scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default&redirect_uri=REGISTERED_URI&state=RANDOM (or use the customer's tenant ID instead of organizations). Don't use common.
On success the redirect carries admin_consent=True and tenant=GUID. Don't trust the tenant value for authentication.

You can also send an admin through the normal authorize URL with prompt=consent and they'll see a consent-on-behalf-of-organization option. Without prompt=consent, an admin's consent covers only their own account.
If the customer has the admin consent workflow enabled, users can request approval from the consent prompt instead.

steps.title: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (optional, for publisher verification)
instructions: As a Global admin of a work-account tenant (not a personal, free-trial or government tenant), join the program in Partner Center and accept the program agreement.
Expect email, identity, employment and business checks, plus uploads of domain and business registration documents.
Verification usually takes 3-5 business days. Track it under Account settings > Legal info until the status is Authorized.
Note the Partner One ID of your Partner global account (PGA). Location IDs can't be used for publisher verification.

steps.title: Set a publisher domain that matches your partner email domain
instructions: On the app's Branding & properties page, set the publisher domain.
It can't be *.onmicrosoft.com. It must match the email domain used for Partner Program verification, or that domain must be a DNS-verified custom domain in your Entra tenant.

steps.title: Mark the app as publisher verified
instructions: Sign in with MFA as an Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator who is also a Partner Admin or Account Admin in Partner Center.
Open the app > Branding & properties > Add Partner ID to verify publisher, enter the Partner One ID and select Verify and save.
It takes a few minutes. A blue verified badge then appears next to the Publisher display name and, after replication, on consent prompts. Test with prompt=consent.

links.label: Mark an app as publisher verified

steps.title: Plan credential rotation
instructions: Record the secret's expiry date and add a new secret (or certificate) before the old one expires. invalid_client means the credentials aren't valid.
Prefer a certificate kept in a key vault for production.

requirements.label: Verified Partner Program account (optional)
requirements.detail: A Partner One ID for the Partner global account (PGA) of a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account that has completed verification. Only needed for publisher verification.
requirements.howToPrepare: Enroll in Partner Center from a work-account tenant and complete business verification before you need the badge.

requirements.label: Publisher domain
requirements.detail: Not *.onmicrosoft.com. Must match the partner verification email domain or be a DNS-verified custom domain on the tenant.
requirements.howToPrepare: Add and DNS-verify your company domain in the Entra tenant that owns the app.

requirements.label: Roles and MFA for the verifier
requirements.detail: Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in Entra plus Partner Admin or Account Admin in Partner Center, signed in with MFA.
requirements.howToPrepare: Have one person hold both role sets, or coordinate between your Entra and Partner Center admins.

requirements.label: Business and domain documents
requirements.detail: Partner Center verification checks that the business is legally registered at its stated address and the contact is an employee. It asks for formation documents and domain registration documents.
requirements.howToPrepare: Gather incorporation or registration documents and domain registrar records that match your partner account details exactly.

requirements.label: Admin onboarding page
requirements.detail: A page or link that sends customer admins through the admin consent endpoint (or authorize with prompt=consent).
requirements.howToPrepare: Build the connect flow and explain which permissions you request and why.

requirements.label: Accept identity platform terms
requirements.detail: The publisher must consent to the Microsoft identity platform for developers Terms of Use for publisher verification.

blockers.fix: Add the exact URI under Authentication > Web

blockers.symptom: User sees Need admin approval or AADSTS90094
blockers.cause: The tenant's consent policy doesn't let users consent to these permissions (Microsoft-managed default excludes Mail.Read and Calendars.Read), user consent is off, or risk-based step-up flagged an unverified multitenant app
blockers.fix: Have a customer admin use your admin consent link, or the user submits an admin consent workflow request. Publisher verification helps only where the tenant's policy allows user consent.
Add offline_access to the scope and repeat the authorize step

blockers.cause: The code expired (about 1 minute) or code_verifier doesn't match
blockers.fix: Start a new /authorize request and send the matching code_verifier

blockers.cause: The client secret expired or is wrong
blockers.fix: Add a new secret or certificate under Certificates & secrets and deploy it

blockers.symptom: 429 Too Many Requests from Graph mail or calendar endpoints
blockers.cause: Over 10,000 requests in 10 minutes or more than 4 concurrent requests for one mailbox
blockers.fix: Back off, cap concurrency at 4 per mailbox, and use $select to cut payloads

blockers.cause: Publisher domain is *.onmicrosoft.com or doesn't match the partner verification email domain, or a location Partner ID was used
blockers.fix: Set a DNS-verified custom domain as the publisher domain and use the PGA Partner One ID

nuances.text: Assume admin consent for Mail.Read and Calendars.Read in new tenants: the default user consent policy blocks them, with no exception for verified publishers.
Older tenants may still allow user consent to mailbox access; new tenants don't by default.

Risk-based step-up consent is on by default. For multitenant apps registered after November 8, 2020 that aren't publisher verified and ask for more than basic sign-in and profile, user consent from other tenants becomes an admin-approval request.

Without publisher verification the consent prompt shows Unverified where the publisher name would go. Verification adds a blue badge. It doesn't certify security; that's Microsoft 365 Certification, a separate optional program.
If an admin signs in without prompt=consent, the consent covers only their own account. Use prompt=consent or the /adminconsent endpoint for tenant-wide consent.
Account type labels vary: Multiple Entra ID tenants and Accounts in any organizational directory are the same setting.

After the first sign-in via /organizations or /common, call the user's tenant endpoint for later token requests, or MSAL misses its cache and prompts again. Key stored data by tid and validate the issuer per tenant.
Refresh tokens expire after 90 days of inactivity and otherwise last until revoked. This can't be configured.
Long-lived CAE access token lifetimes are given as 20-28 hours on the access tokens page and 24-28 hours on the configurable lifetimes page.
Microsoft prefers 127.0.0.1 over localhost, but the portal won't accept an http 127.0.0.1 redirect URI; you have to edit the manifest. IPv6 [::1] isn't supported.

Users can remove the app at myapps.microsoft.com. If an admin consented for the whole tenant, only an admin can revoke it. Admin password resets in the Entra admin center revoke confidential-client refresh tokens.
Microsoft 365 Publisher Attestation is required for Teams apps, not for a SaaS app using delegated Graph mail and calendar access.

claims.statement: For multitenant apps, an admin sign-in with prompt=consent grants tenant-wide consent; without it, the admin's consent applies only to their own account. On first consent a service principal is created in the customer tenant.

claims.statement: Requesting later tokens via /common for an already signed-in user misses MSAL's cache because tokens are cached per tenant; use the tenant's endpoint for subsequent calls.
claims.label: verified

claims.statement: Users can revoke an app at myapps.microsoft.com; admins revoke via Enterprise applications; if an admin consented for all users, users can't revoke individually.
claims.label: verified

claims.statement: Microsoft presents publisher verification as a program with benefits (badge, smoother adoption) rather than a prerequisite; unverified apps can still be consented to, since risky or admin-only requests step up to admin consent rather than being refused.
claims.label: verified

claims.statement: Publisher verification requires: a Partner One ID for a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner global account (not a location ID); an app registered with an Entra work/school account in a tenant associated with the PGA; a publisher domain that isn't *.onmicrosoft.com and matches the verification email domain or a DNS-verified custom domain; a user with Application Admin or Cloud Application Admin plus Partner Admin or Account Admin roles signing in with MFA; and acceptance of the identity platform Terms of Use.
claims.label: verified

claims.statement: Microsoft doesn't charge for publisher verification, no license is required, and there are no charges for completing its prerequisites.
claims.label: verified

sources.title: Publisher verification overview
sources.quote: Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification.

claims.statement: Developers who already meet the requirements can be verified in minutes; the request may take a few minutes and the badge replicates to consent prompts afterwards.
claims.label: verified

sources.title: Mark an app as publisher verified

claims.statement: The verified badge doesn't indicate quality, certifications or compliance; Microsoft 365 App Certification covers that.
claims.label: verified

claims.statement: To verify: sign in with MFA, App registrations > app > Branding & properties, make sure the publisher domain is set and matches, select Add Partner ID to verify publisher, enter the Partner ID, Verify and save; a blue badge appears next to Publisher display name.
claims.label: verified

sources.title: Mark an app as publisher verified

claims.statement: Partner Program enrollment needs a Global admin of a work-account tenant (not personal, free-trial or government tenants) with authority to sign agreements who can produce legal documents; it creates a PGA and a location account.
claims.label: verified

sources.title: How to enroll in partner program

claims.statement: Partner Center verification includes email, identity (government-issued document), employment (domain documentation) and business verification (legal registration at the stated address, with formation documents), plus possible additional checks.
claims.label: verified

sources.title: Understand the verification process in Partner Center

claims.statement: Microsoft says Partner Center verification takes three to five business days in most cases, longer if additional review is needed.
claims.label: verified

sources.title: Understand the verification process in Partner Center
sources.quote: In most cases, the process takes three to five business days

claims.statement: Microsoft 365 Publisher Attestation is a self-assessment questionnaire in Partner Center, renewed yearly, described as a requirement for all Teams apps and a prerequisite for Microsoft 365 Certification.
claims.label: verified

claims.statement: An MVP answered (June 2025) that for a multitenant mail app, publisher verification can be a blocker: an admin in the other organization can still grant consent, but end users can't.
claims.label: reported

claims.statement: An email API vendor's guide says users see Need admin approval when the app needs administrator consent and advises completing publisher verification in addition to domain verification.
claims.label: reported

claims.statement: A developer reported (March 2026) being unable to enroll in the Partner Program to verify an Outlook app; the accepted answer was AI-generated and didn't address individuals without a registered business.
claims.label: reported
